correctness.rationale: Fix any integer n>=4 and n distinct complex lines with no triple concurrency. The reciprocal map is defined by omitted-factor products; its base ideal is the reduced intersection-point ideal with local generators the two transverse line parameters. After blowing up its binomial(n,2) points, each strict line transform is a smooth rational -(n-2) curve, every point-blowup exceptional maps isomorphically to the appropriate coordinate line, and the map is birational and resolves the previously known isolated singular support. At vertex p_i, write ell_j=alpha_j u+L_j(v,w) and y_j=u/ell_j; the invertible local change z_j=y_j/(1-alpha_j*y_j) gives exactly z_j=u/L_j. The n-1 products Q_j=prod_{k != i,j} L_k are linearly independent as degree n-2 binary forms by evaluation at their distinct omitted zeros, hence are a basis of H0(P1,O(n-2)). The local image closure is therefore the entire Veronese cone C[s,t]^(n-2), proving full completed local-ring equality. Toric divisor exact sequences give Cl=Z/(n-2), the cone degree gives multiplicity n-2, and quotient determinant weight 2 gives local Gorenstein index (n-2)/gcd(n-2,2). Adjunction and toric valuation comparison yield mld=2/(n-2), with discrepancy 2/(n-2)-1; no exceptional (-1) curve remains. Independent exact-rational symbolic-instance checks of 60 chart polynomial bases and local substitutions at n=4..11 succeeded. Those finite computations supplement, rather than substitute for, the proof.

originality.rationale: The surviving novelty claim is the explicit nonlinear analytic isomorphism of the completed local reciprocal-plane vertex germ to the full Veronese quotient and the resulting uniform cyclic-quotient, divisor-class, canonical-index and minimal-log-discrepancy classification. Prior reciprocal-plane tangent cones and reduced singular support (Sanyal–Sturmfels–Vinzant) and the blowup of line intersections with contractions of the arrangement lines (Schenck, Theorem 3.4) are fully credited and are not counted as original. This stronger local analytic theorem was not stated in the materially inspected sources; potential unindexed prior specialization remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A local analytic quotient normal form may have appeared in unindexed reciprocal-plane, star-configuration or plane Cremona-transformation literature.
The 2017 Rees-algebra framework already gives the graph blowup, so its bare existence has no novelty; the claimed extra content is the full singularity and contraction classification.
The known 2011 theorem already implies the tangent-cone type, support and multiplicity; these are included only as proved context, not priority claims.
No independent specialist audit or exhaustive global literature survey was conducted.

The classical single (-r)-curve resolution description may allow an expert to deduce the cyclic quotient type by standard surface theory; the present explicit nonlinear local-ring isomorphism and systematic local invariant formulation could therefore be judged an accessible corollary rather than a major independent theorem.

value.rationale: The uniform completed-local-ring isomorphism is stronger than a known tangent-cone theorem and is furnished by an explicit nonlinear coordinate change for every general-position rank-three line arrangement. It determines pointwise cyclic quotient type and the associated local class group Z/(n-2), Gorenstein index (n-2)/gcd(n-2,2) and mld 2/(n-2), including a meaningful canonical-to-noncanonical boundary. This is a natural complete analytic singularity classification for a classical family, with reproducible explicit coordinates and local birational invariants, rather than an arbitrary finite slice. The already published global blowup geometry is used as an input, not sold as new.
